seo.title: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Finchampstead | Fit-Only Installation | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: The sanitaryware, brassware and tile brands we fit for Finchampstead clients, and how our fit-only installation model works alongside your own supplier choices.

h1: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Finchampstead

hero.intro: We don't sell bathrooms in Finchampstead — we fit them. That's the fit-only model in a sentence: you choose and buy your own sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture, from whichever showroom or retailer you prefer, and we install it to the standard the brand and your room both deserve. Over 30 years of fitting high-end bathrooms, certain brands turn up on our Finchampstead specification sheets more often than others — some suited to the solid masonry and suspended timber floors of the older buildings near the village core, others just as at home in the post-war and more modern housing spreading out towards Wokingham, Crowthorne and Finchampstead Ridges — each with its own installation detail that matters more than most people expect before the first fixing goes into the wall.

sections.heading: The fit-only model explained
sections.body: Nothing about the fit-only model changes which brands you can bring to a Finchampstead installation — if anything, it widens the choice, because we're not trying to steer you toward stock we hold or a supplier we have an arrangement with. You buy from the showroom or retailer you trust, at the price you've agreed, and we check it all at survey: waste sizes, tap centres, fixing requirements and whether everything you've chosen is actually compatible with everything else, before strip-out starts rather than after a delivery is already sitting in the hallway.

sections.heading: Sanitaryware and shower toilets we fit
sections.body: Geberit's concealed cisterns, wall-hung WCs and AquaClean shower toilets are among the sanitaryware we fit most often in Finchampstead, and correct frame selection matters more here than with most brands, because the cistern and pan weight sits entirely on the carrier frame rather than the wall tiles — a detail worth getting right in an older masonry-walled house near the village core as much as a newer, post-war one. Where Duravit is specified, it's usually alongside SensoWash shower toilet seats or a full ME by Starck suite, and the detail worth settling early is whether the installation route is Duravit's own DuraSystem frame or a standard concealed cistern frame — the two aren't interchangeable once a wall is boarded. Laufen's SaphirKeramik material lets it produce basins and pans with noticeably finer rims and sharper geometry than standard vitreous china allows, which is a strong material once fitted and fixed, but the pieces are less forgiving of a knock in transit or on site, so handling and sequencing get more attention than with a heavier, more conventional basin.

sections.heading: Brassware and showers we fit
sections.body: hansgrohe brassware and shower systems appear on a good number of our Finchampstead specification sheets, usually paired with sanitaryware from Duravit or Laufen — the engineering is consistent, so performance comes down to water pressure, rough-in depth and whether the valve body was set correctly before the wall closed up. Grohe covers a wide span of the work we do here too, from thermostatic shower valves and mixer taps on mid-range refits through to Rapid SL cistern frames and digital shower products on more specified projects, which is why we work through exactly what's been chosen at survey rather than treating every Grohe job the same way. Crosswater's contemporary brassware and shower systems run heavily on concealed valves, digital controls and minimal deck-mounted taps, which means the work that determines how well a Crosswater shower performs happens largely before the tiler arrives — wall build-up, pipework depth, and the water pressure and flow the valve actually needs.

sections.heading: Baths, trays and tiling brands we fit
sections.body: Bette manufactures baths and shower trays from titanium-steel finished with fused glass enamel — harder and more scratch-resistant than acrylic, but unforgiving of a poorly built base underneath it, so we fit Bette with the substructure, levelling and acoustic isolation the material actually needs rather than treating it like any other bath. Kaldewei's titanium-enamelled steel baths and shower trays are similarly rigid rather than flexible, so the installation detail is about even, accurate bearing across the full base rather than preventing flex. For tiling, Porcelanosa's large-format porcelain is dense, rectified and dimensionally precise, which punishes an uneven substrate or an inconsistent joint far more visibly than a smaller, more forgiving tile would — we check the floor or wall is flat first, then set the tile with the correct bed coverage, joint width and lippage control to let the material's own precision show through. Matki's largely frameless shower enclosures leave very little trim to hide an inaccurate opening, so measuring, wall fixing and sequencing against tiling and the tray get planned in that order, not worked out on the day.

sections.heading: Choosing brands for Finchampstead's older and post-war homes
sections.body: Finchampstead's village core carries a number of older buildings with solid masonry walls and, on the ground floor, a higher chance of suspended timber construction, while the wider area spreading towards Wokingham, Crowthorne and up towards Finchampstead Ridges is largely post-war and more modern housing on a solid concrete slab. That mix doesn't dictate which brands suit which property — a Geberit frame or a Matki frameless screen fits into an older village-core house as readily as a post-war home once the wall or floor underneath has been properly checked — but it does change what gets checked first. A rigid Kaldewei or Bette steel bath, or a heavier Porcelanosa porcelain floor, needs an older suspended timber floor confirmed for deflection before it goes anywhere near the room, which is exactly what the survey is for, whichever brand ends up being specified.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy my bathroom from you?
faqs.a: No. We're fit-only — you buy your sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture from whichever showroom or retailer you choose, and we install it.

faqs.q: Can you fit a bathroom with products from several different brands mixed together?
faqs.a: Yes, this is the norm. We check waste sizes, tap centres and fixing requirements across every brand involved at survey, so everything is confirmed compatible before strip-out starts.

faqs.q: Do you have a preferred brand you push clients toward?
faqs.a: No. The fit-only model means we don't hold stock or have a sales arrangement with any particular manufacturer — the brands mentioned here are simply the ones that appear most often on the specifications our Finchampstead clients bring to us.

faqs.q: Does an older Finchampstead property near the village core limit which brands I can fit?
faqs.a: No, but it does change what we check first. Solid masonry walls and suspended timber floors are common in the village core, so we confirm fixing and floor deflection at survey before a heavy bath, basin or large-format tile is ordered, regardless of brand.

faqs.q: Does a heavy freestanding bath need anything extra checking in an older Finchampstead house?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A Bette or Kaldewei steel bath has real weight and needs accurate, even bearing underneath it — on a ground floor with suspended timber construction, we confirm that structural support at survey before the bath is ordered.

faqs.q: Will you fit products bought from an online retailer rather than a showroom?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the specification is confirmed compatible at survey. We check this regardless of where a product was bought from.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Finchampstead brands page, a close/mid detail shot implying a choice between brands rather than a full room. Subject and action: a travertine-topped vanity carrying a sleek wall-mounted basin mixer tap on one side, with a stack of large-format porcelain tile samples leaning against the vanity edge on the other, as if mid-way through a specification decision, no running water. Setting and work-stage: a finished bathroom corner inside a renovated Finchampstead house, midday, bright daylight entering from an unseen side window. Composition: close-to-fixture mid shot centred on the vanity edge where the tap meets the travertine surface, tile samples filling the lower-right foreground, softly blurred wall tiling in the background. Light and materials: honed travertine vanity top with natural pitting and warm tonal variation, brushed brass basin mixer tap, pale large-format porcelain tile samples leaning against the stone, bright midday daylight raking across the travertine at a shallow angle, creating uneven highlight and shadow rather than flat light. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on any fixture or tile; no LED lighting strips anywhere in frame; no symmetrical twin-basin staging; no uniform gold or amber colour wash; no hanging plants, florals or candles; no water shown running; fixtures should show faint, believable handling marks rather than uniform showroom-new gloss.
